comparator.sourceNotes: The 180 EC curriculum combines Greek and Latin language and reading with ancient history, archaeology, philosophy and research. The example follows the language proficiency courses for students who took both languages in their school exams. A transition module replaces the proficiency assessment in each language where needed.

exception.reason: UCR offers substantial study of Greek archaeology, ancient democracy, myth and classical rhetoric. A full UCR programme built around these courses would move into broader literature, art or politics before developing the sustained study of Greek and Roman texts, history and material culture that defines Groningen Classics.
exception.curriculumContext: The ordinary full-time programme has 60 EC each year, including a 10 EC faculty-wide choice, a 30 EC minor and a required 10 EC thesis. Two language research seminars follow the first-year foundation.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: The Greek archaeology and democracy courses develop ancient material and political inquiry. Comparative myth and literary courses include classical works, and rhetoric teaches Greek and Roman practice. General or modern research and reception courses broaden these studies but do not establish sustained research in Greek and Roman texts, historical sources and material culture together.

candidateAssessment.label: Classical antiquity through literature, rhetoric, philosophy & archaeology
candidateAssessment.reason: The humanities composition has valuable Greek archaeology, myth, classical rhetoric and philosophy. Its advanced work concentrates on broader literature, art, media and modern history, with little continuity in specialist Classics research.

candidateAssessment.label: Antiquity, democracy & political traditions
candidateAssessment.reason: The second composition begins with Athenian democracy, political philosophy and archaeology. Its later focus is on comparative politics, international and constitutional law, and modern institutions.

audience.programmeDescription: Classics at the University of Groningen combines Greek and Latin language and literature with ancient history, archaeology and philosophy. Students learn to interpret original texts and investigate the ancient world through several kinds of evidence.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial study of Greek archaeology, ancient democracy, myth and classical rhetoric. A full UCR programme built around these courses would move into broader literature, art or politics before developing the sustained study of Greek and Roman texts, history and material culture that defines Groningen Classics.
